findings.description: The security group allows SSH (port 22) ingress from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port of the instance to the entire internet, and also allows HTTP from 0.0.0.0/0 without any compensating controls (e.g. no HTTPS/TLS).
The security group's egress rule permits all outbound traffic on all ports/protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration path.

AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance's user_data script, which is readable by anyone with DescribeInstanceAttribute permissions and is stored in plaintext in the Terraform state/config.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true nor specify a KMS key, leaving the data at rest unencrypted by default.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving sensitive network flow data unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / public access block
findings.description: The bucket has no public access block, versioning, or bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled, increasing risk of accidental exposure or deletion of audit log data.
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched here, increasing exposure of the web server and any future instances.
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to any instances launched in this subnet, expanding the attack surface unnecessarily.
The instance does not configure metadata_options to require IMDSv2 (http_tokens = required), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled and vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft.
Root/attached volume lacks a customer-managed KMS key configuration, meaning even if encryption were enabled it would rely on default keys rather than explicit key management controls.
